Water damage is one of those "install a sensor and save yourself a fortune in repairs" problems, whether it's the floor or the cabinetry. Leak sensors have long been one of the best-value products in the smart home, and Shelly's new Flood S Gen4 makes getting started even easier. It costs under US$30, is Matter-certified, and supports Apple Home right out of the box.

HomeKit Weekly is a column series dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Larger Sensing Surface

Most leak sensors on the market use small metal probes on the bottom, meaning water has to pool in exactly the right spot to trigger them. Shelly's new sensor takes a different approach, with three large stainless-steel sensing pads distributed across the underside of the device. The much larger contact area means water can be detected faster and in more locations—which is precisely why you'd place a sensor under your water heater or washing machine.

These sensing pads are also sensitive enough to detect clean or low-conductivity water, such as condensate from an air conditioner. These kinds of leaks are often harder to spot. The Flood S Gen4 is also slim enough to slide under appliances, behind toilets, and beneath sink basins—exactly where you'd most want to place a device like this.

Matter / Apple Home Support

The Flood S Gen4 is Matter-certified, supports both Wi-Fi and Zigbee, and works with Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, SmartThings, and Home Assistant. Once added to Apple Home, the automation possibilities expand dramatically:

  • Instantly cut power to the washing machine or dishwasher (if plugged into a smart outlet) the moment water is detected
  • Trigger all the smart bulbs in the home
  • Simple, straightforward leak alerts on your iPhone (especially useful when you're away from home)

Modes, Alerts, and Battery Life

The device has a built-in local alarm, so besides phone notifications, people in the home will hear it even if the phone is in another room. Shelly offers two operating modes—flood detection and rain detection—plus three alert settings (Strong, Normal, and Economy), letting you balance leak detection speed against battery life. The included CR123A battery can last up to two years.

Wrap-Up

At under US$30, this is the kind of accessory you'll buy three or four of without thinking twice. One in front of the water heater, one in front of the dishwasher, one under the washing machine, one under the kitchen sink. Matter / Apple Home support means you can receive alerts via the Home app and build Apple Home automations around it. There's a lot to like about this product, and I can't find anything I don't like. Trust me, buying a flood sensor is the smartest investment you can make for your smart home.

You can buy the Shelly Flood S Gen4 directly from Amazon or the Shelly website.
